content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% if sentiment is negative or neutral.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overreact with sharp upward moves; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below recent high or adjust downward by 3–6% for each negative sentiment point.
- Model underestimates downward trends after strong recent highs; if sentiment is negative and price drops >5% from recent peak, forecast should be adjusted downward by 2–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing short-term sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, adjust forecast 3–5 days ahead by -1–2% per day to reflect mean reversion.
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., +10–15% above recent high) is common; if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, reduce forecast by 5–10% after spike to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; if sentiment > 0.2 and price is declining, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes or price stabilizes.
